ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Here is a sketch that shows Earth’s water cycle including the oceans and continents. Assuming that total precipitation equals total evaporation, what is the value of evaporation from the land to the atmosphere?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The title in the figure is “Earth’s Water Cycle”. Above the land on the left there is a downward arrow labeled “Precipitation 107 × 10^15 kg/yr”, and above the ocean on the right there is a downward arrow labeled “Precipitation 398 × 10^15 kg/yr”. There is an upward arrow from the ocean labeled “Evaporation 434 × 10^15 kg/yr”, and there is an upward arrow from the land labeled “Evaporation ?”. Then reason: The question says total precipitation equals total evaporation, so first add the two precipitation amounts, 107 + 398 = 505 (the units are all ×10^15 kg/yr). The ocean evaporation is known to be 434 × 10^15 kg/yr, therefore land evaporation = total evaporation − ocean evaporation = 505 − 434 = 71 × 10^15 kg/yr.

raw_record.question_text: Here is a sketch that shows Earth’s water cycle including the oceans and continents. Assuming that total precipitation equals total evaporation, what is the value of evaporation from the land to the atmosphere?

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram and note the four relevant fluxes. Add the precipitation values shown in the image: 107 × 10^15 + 398 × 10^15 = 505 × 10^15 kg/yr. Then add the known evaporation from the oceans: 434 × 10^15 kg/yr. Because the problem states total precipitation equals total evaporation, set 434 + land evaporation = 505. Solve by subtraction: land evaporation = 505 - 434 = 71 × 10^15 kg/yr, so the answer is 71e15.
